headline: 15-month-olds to get typhoid vaccines from August 1
summary: The government has added the Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV) to the routine immunisation programme to protect children from life-threatening bacterial infections.
details: The government has decided to add the Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV) to the country’s routine immunisation programme starting August 1.
All children aged exactly 15 months will receive a dose of the TCV through the Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI).
The vaccine may be administered simultaneously with the second dose of the measles-rubella (MR-2) vaccine during the same vaccination season.
This decision follows a review of the latest scientific evidence regarding the vaccine’s effectiveness and its disease-prevention capacity.
The government had previously implemented a nationwide TCV campaign last year.
Integrating the vaccine into the routine programme aims to strengthen protection and establish sustainable disease prevention for children.
With the inclusion of TCV, the total number of vaccines under the routine immunisation programme has increased to nine, according to Hasanul Mahmud, assistant director of EPI.
caption:
Starting August 1, all 15-month-old children in Bangladesh will receive the typhoid vaccine as part of routine immunisation.

The government has decided to add the Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV) to the country’s routine immunisation programme starting August 1.

All children aged exactly 15 months will receive a dose of the TCV through the Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI).

The vaccine may be administered simultaneously with the second dose of the measles-rubella (MR-2) vaccine during the same vaccination season.

This decision follows a review of the latest scientific evidence regarding the vaccine’s effectiveness and its disease-prevention capacity.

The government had previously implemented a nationwide TCV campaign last year.

Integrating the vaccine into the routine programme aims to strengthen protection and establish sustainable disease prevention for children.

With the inclusion of TCV, the total number of vaccines under the routine immunisation programme has increased to nine, according to Hasanul Mahmud, assistant director of EPI.

headline: Rainwater leaks from roof: Students take exams under umbrellas indoors
summary: Students are forced to use umbrellas inside their classroom to protect themselves and their answer scripts from leaking roofs during an exam.
details: Students are taking their examinations while holding umbrellas over their heads inside the classroom.
The situation arose because rainwater is leaking through the roof of the school building, making it impossible to sit for the exam without protection.
The images show students focused on their papers while sheltered under various colorful umbrellas to keep their scripts dry.
This highlights the poor infrastructure and lack of maintenance of the school building, forcing students to adapt in extreme conditions to complete their academic requirements.
